{{Short description|Analytic number theory}}
{{CS1 config|mode=cs2}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''Hardy–Ramanujan theorem''', proved by [[Srinivasa Ramanujan|Ramanujan]] and checked by [[G. H. Hardy|Hardy]]<ref>{{citation|first1=G. H.|last1= Hardy| authorlink=G. H. Hardy| first2= S.|last2=Ramanujan| authorlink2=Srinivasa Ramanujan |title=The normal number of prime factors of a number ''n''| journal= Quarterly Journal of Mathematics |volume= 48  |year=1917|pages= 76–92 | url=http://www.imsc.res.in/~rao/ramanujan/CamUnivCpapers/Cpaper35/page1.htm | jfm=46.0262.03 }}</ref> states  that the [[Normal order of an arithmetic function|normal order]] of the number <math>\omega(n)</math> of distinct [[prime factor]]s of a number <math>n</math> is <math>\log\log n</math>.

Roughly speaking, this means that most numbers have about this number of distinct prime factors.

==Precise statement==
A more precise version<ref>{{citation
 | last = Heath-Brown | first = D. R.
 | doi = 10.46298/hrj.2007.156
 | journal = Hardy–Ramanujan Journal
 | mr = 2440316
 | pages = 6–12
 | title = Carmichael numbers with three prime factors
 | volume = 30
 | year = 2007
 | article-number = 156
 }}</ref> states that for every real-valued function <math>\psi(n)</math> that tends to infinity as <math>n</math> tends to infinity
<math display=block>|\omega(n)-\log\log n|<\psi(n)\sqrt{\log\log n}</math>
or more traditionally
<math display=block>|\omega(n)-\log\log n|<{(\log\log n)}^{\frac12 +\varepsilon}</math> 
for ''[[almost all]]'' (all but an [[infinitesimal]] proportion of) integers.  That is, let <math>g(x)</math> be the number of positive integers <math>n</math> less than <math>x</math> for which the above inequality fails: then <math>g(x)/x</math> converges to zero as <math>x</math> goes to infinity.

==History==
A simple proof to the result was given by [[Pál Turán]], who used the [[Turán sieve]] to prove that<ref>{{citation | last=Turán | first=Pál | authorlink=Pál Turán | title=On a theorem of Hardy and Ramanujan | journal=Journal of the London Mathematical Society | volume=9 | issue=4 | pages=274–276 | year=1934 | issn=0024-6107 | zbl=0010.10401 | doi = 10.1112/jlms/s1-9.4.274 }}</ref>

<math display=block>\sum_{n \le x} | \omega(n) - \log\log x|^2 \ll x \log\log x . </math>

==Generalizations==
The same results are true of <math>\Omega(n)</math>, the number of prime factors of <math>n</math> counted with [[Multiplicity (mathematics)#Multiplicity of a prime factor|multiplicity]].
This theorem is generalized by the [[Erdős–Kac theorem]], which shows that <math>\omega(n)</math> is essentially [[Normal distribution|normally distributed]]. There are many proofs of this, including the method of moments (Granville & Soundararajan)<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Granville | first1 = Andrew
 | last2 = Soundararajan | first2 = K.
 | editor1-last = Granville | editor1-first = Andrew
 | editor2-last = Rudnick | editor2-first = Zeév
 | arxiv = math/0606039
 | contribution = Sieving and the Erdős-Kac theorem
 | doi = 10.1007/978-1-4020-5404-4_2
 | isbn = 978-1-4020-5403-7
 | mr = 2290492
 | pages = 15–27
 | publisher = Springer | location = Dordrecht
 | series = NATO Science Series II: Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry
 | title = Equidistribution in number theory, an introduction: Proceedings of the NATO Advanced Study Institute (the 44th Séminaire de Mathématiques Supérieures (SMS)) held at the Université de Montréal, Montréal, QC, July 11–22, 2005
 | volume = 237
 | year = 2007}}</ref> and [[Stein's method]] (Harper).<ref>{{citation
 | last = Harper | first = Adam J.
 | doi = 10.1017/S0305004109002412
 | issue = 1
 | journal = [[Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society]]
 | mr = 2507311
 | pages = 95–114
 | title = Two new proofs of the Erdős-Kac theorem, with bound on the rate of convergence, by Stein's method for distributional approximations
 | volume = 147
 | year = 2009
 | bibcode = 2009MPCPS.147...95H
 }}</ref> It was shown by Durkan that a modified version of Turán's result allows one to prove the Hardy–Ramanujan Theorem with any even moment.<ref>{{cite arXiv |last=Durkan |first=Benjamin |title=On the Hardy–Ramanujan Theorem |date=2023-10-23 |class=math.NT |eprint=2310.14760}}</ref>
